Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Helio MSA redline: training carveout and productization

Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helio is keen to move forward but Legal has pushed back on a couple of core items in the MSA/order form. I attached our redlines (see Helio_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf). The two points that are blockers for us:

1) Training / Model Use: We require an explicit carveout that prohibits Redwood from using Helio customer data or Helio-generated outputs to train or improve any models that are used to serve other customers.

2) Productization / Derivative Use: Helio requires customer ownership of outputs and an additional clause that prevents Redwood from creating products derived from Helio outputs (i.e., no downstream productization by Redwood or its partners).

We are open to a limited feedback channel but want a clear, time-bound opt-in so Helio can control any usage of its data.

We need these resolved before procurement will sign. Can you loop in legal?

Thanks,
Diana Morris
Head of Procurement — Helio Platform

Subject: Re: Helio MSA redline: training carveout and productization — legal take

Connor / Laura — I reviewed Helio's redlines. Key points and proposed positions below (high level):

- Absolute ban on training: we can't accept wording that prevents Redwood from using aggregated, de-identified telemetry or outputs to improve model quality; that would materially impact platform safety and cost. Instead propose two options: 1) carveout allowing "aggregated, de-identified improvements" with a robust definition, or 2) contract-level feature: a paid Customer Opt-Out from training (we can accept for order-forms over an ARR threshold with pricing uplift).

- Output ownership vs productization: we can agree that Helio has broad rights to use outputs (including commercial use), but must retain a prohibition on using customer outputs to create a product that competes with Helio or to train models that are then sold to other customers. Suggested language: "Customer owns Outputs for their business purposes; Redwood shall not incorporate Customer Outputs into a model offered as a standalone product to third parties without Customer's prior written consent."

- Feedback license: propose a limited, non-exclusive, perpetual license to use feedback (logs, error reports) for improving services, with an option for Helio to opt-out of feedback collection on a 30-day notice. Also propose a 12-month retention for audit logs unless otherwise required.

I've drafted suggested redline language and a short rationale doc: Proposed_ML_Carveouts.docx (attached). If the customer insists on the absolute training ban we can escalate commercially (opt-out + price).

I'll be on the 10/3 sync.

— Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Karthik's summary (high level):
- We can grant Helio ownership and commercial rights to Outputs for Helio's business use.
- We will not use Customer Outputs to create a product that competes with Helio or for sale to third parties without consent.
- For training: propose a narrow definition of "Training" and allow Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified signals. Alternatively, Helio may elect a paid Opt-Out to prohibit training on Helio data/outputs entirely.
- Feedback license: propose a limited license to use submitted feedback for service improvement; provide a 30-day opt-out mechanism and 12-month retention for related telemetry.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call to confirm trade-offs; if Helio prefers an absolute training ban we will need to convert that to a commercial opt-out with adjusted pricing.

----

Would 10/3 at 11:00am PT work for a quick alignment call? If not, please propose an alternative.

Connor

Subject: Re: Helio MSA redline: training carveout and productization — next steps

Connor / Karthik / Laura — thanks for the clear approach. Procurement reviewed the compromise and Helio is prepared to accept the following with one final tweak:

1) Helio accepts the "aggregated, de-identified" carveout for platform improvements (we will review the definition you propose).
2) Helio requires the non-compete productization language you suggested — that is acceptable.
3) Feedback license: Helio will opt-in for a pilot but requires a 30-day sunset after pilot completion unless we explicitly renew; also request a right to audit logs related to any use of Helio Outputs for model improvements (audit limited to scope/time and performed under NDA).

If you can incorporate the audit clause and the 30-day sunset into the redline, procurement can issue a final sign-off. Please send an updated MSA redline (track changes preferred) and we will route for signature.

Appreciate the trade space here — let's try to get the final redline by end of week.

Best,
Diana Morris
Head of Procurement — Helio Platform
